Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The study focuses on the development of a customizable virtual human (CVH) and a 3D hand-eye coordination training game for adolescents with ASD. The primary goal is to investigate the effects of CVH on performance and user experience. The design process emphasizes utility first, as it aims to improve hand-eye coordination and performance in a training game, with customization features added to enhance motivation and user experience. This aligns with option (4) 'mostly utility first'.

        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The context describes a study involving a game with specific rules and structured sessions. Participants were instructed to play as many rounds as possible within a session and were rewarded for playing more rounds. They could control the pace of the game by adjusting their walking/running speed. In study part 2, participants had the freedom to play any number of sessions without time limits, but they were required to play at least one kick-block under both conditions (NCVH and CVH). The game involved specific tasks and rules, such as blocking a ball, which indicates a structured and rule-based environment. These details suggest that the design of the study aligns with a game that has rigid rules, similar to a video game.

reasoning: The context describes a study where participants played a game with both time-limited and free-play sessions. In the free-play sessions, participants had no time limits and could choose to play with either a customizable virtual human (CVH) or a non-customizable virtual human (NCVH). This indicates a mix of synchronous (time-limited) and asynchronous (free-play) affordances.
